title: GraphQL schema disclosure: introspection or error suggestions map the hidden attack surface
index_line: T-0013 · INFO_LEAK · __schema dump / typo-suggestion enumeration → authz targets · corroborated
invariant_violated: The app hides admin objects behind authz checks but leaves the schema discoverable — introspection enabled, or error suggestions that enumerate it.

mechanism.does: attacker sends a crafted GraphQL query ({__typename} to confirm the endpoint)
schema lookup via __schema/__type — or, with introspection off, typo-suggestion enumeration ('Did you mean…?')
full attack surface disclosed: admin mutations, password/secret/token fields, Debug/InternalUser types, ID arguments
leaked schema becomes the authz-gap target list: per-field object-level checks, batch auth bypass, IDOR arguments

encoding.graphql.value: {__schema{types{name fields{name args{name}}}}} · {__type(name:"User")…} · {userr} suggestion abuse · alias batches a1:… a1000:

guard.introspection.value: introspection disabled? then the question is whether error suggestions still enumerate

oracle.error.value: Did-you-mean suggestions and resolver errors as the enumeration oracle

preconditions.expr: GraphQL server library in the tree
endpoint reachable without prior auth (or with the lowest auth tier)
varies — many deployments expose the endpoint pre-auth

success: typo query yields 'Did you mean' suggestions with introspection disabled
admin mutation names and password/secret fields present in the dumped schema
failure_like: introspection disabled AND suggestions suppressed — only blind guessing remains
depth/complexity limits resist the DoS flavors (separate concern)
false_positive: GraphiQL left on but every mutation correctly authz-checked — exposure without a gap is a low-severity config finding, not this record's claim
public API whose schema is published by design

hazards: introspection maps the surface; the finding is the authz gap it reveals — test every admin mutation and ID argument
batching/alias rate-limit bypass and nested DoS are adjacent records, not this one
non_transfers: endpoints requiring introspection-independent auth before any query
